title: Beirut Stock Exchange founded under French Mandate
why: Established by decree of the French commissioner; trading later halted in 1983 and relaunched in 1996.

title: Beirut hosts 39 newspapers and 137 periodicals
why: By the 1940s the city had a dense multilingual press, the base of its later publishing-hub role.

title: Middle East Airlines established
why: Founded 31 May 1945; began operations 1 January 1946.

title: AUB establishes a dedicated School of Engineering
why: Civil, mechanical, electrical and architectural curricula; engineering courses had been taught at AUB since 1913.

title: Intra Bank founded
why: Grew into Lebanon's largest bank, controlling MEA and Casino du Liban until its 1966 collapse.

title: Lebanese University established
why: Created after a student strike of January 1951; Lebanon's first public university.

title: Dar Al-Adab publishing house founded in Beirut
why: Suhail Idriss's house; one search summary gives 1953, another ties the founding to 1956, so the year is uncertain. Dar Al Adab site: founded 1956 by Souheil Idriss; the magazine Al-Adab dates to 1953 (corrected from 1953)

title: Beirut international airport opens at Khalde
why: Replaced the smaller Bir Hassan airfield; later renamed Rafic Hariri International.

title: Beirut holds the Arab world's first book fair
why: Cited as evidence of the city's publishing-hub role.

title: Government grants first TV licence to Izzeddine and Moufarrej
why: Licence led to Compagnie Libanaise de Télévision (CLT).

title: Banking secrecy law signed to attract Arab deposits
why: Numbered accounts and customer confidentiality, Swiss-style, aimed at Gulf and expatriate capital.

title: Shi'r magazine founded in Beirut by Yusuf al-Khal
why: Founded with Adonis and Ounsi el-Hajj; drove Arabic poetic modernism; ran 1957-1970 with a gap.

title: Casino du Liban opens
why: Tourism and entertainment landmark; closed 1989, reopened 1996 after a $50m refit. Year only confirmed.

title: CLT begins broadcasting: first commercial TV in the Arab world
why: Iraq's state TV began 2 May 1956, so CLT is first commercial or private, not first overall.

title: Haigazian College Rocket Society formed
why: Manoug Manougian and students began rocket research on a LBP 750 grant.

title: MEA receives its first jet, a Comet 4C
why: First of four de Havilland Comet 4Cs arrived 15 December 1960.

title: First single-stage rocket reaches about 1 km
why: After failures; later improvements took altitude to 2 km.

title: Télé Orient obtains second TV licence
why: Competitor to CLT, operating from Hazmieh; the two merged in 1977.

title: Press law takes effect under President Chehab
why: Regulated Lebanon's press; remained the framework through at least 2013.

title: HCRS-7 Cedar launched; Lebanese Rocket Society follows
why: Reached 11.5 km with Army security; further Cedar launches that summer reached 20 km.

title: Cedar IV launched, reported at 140 km altitude
why: Wikipedia says 90 miles; the article is single-sourced with citation flags, so treat altitude as unverified.

title: Banque du Liban created by Code of Money and Credit
why: Began operating effectively on 1 April 1964.

title: Launch accident hospitalises two students
why: Summer 1964 accident; sources link it to the wind-down of the rocket programme.

title: Final Cedar rocket launch
why: Programme ended; one account cites French and Western pressure, not confirmed by a primary source.

title: Intra Bank collapses
why: Sources give 14 or 15 October 1966; it held 15% of all bank deposits.

title: CLT among first in world to broadcast in colour (SECAM)
why: Described as the third country to broadcast in colour using French SECAM.

title: Israeli raid destroys aircraft at Beirut airport
why: Commandos destroyed 14 civilian aircraft, including much of MEA's fleet.

title: State founds Ogero, fixed-line telecom operator
why: Later ran backbone, DSL and ISP services.

title: Civil war begins
why: War lasted to October 1990; effect on Beirut's hub role is inference, not from the source.

title: Decree merges CLT and Télé Orient into Télé Liban
why: Legislative Decree 100 made the merger official after war-time losses.

title: Beirut Stock Exchange trading halted
why: Meant to be temporary; lasted over a decade.

title: LBC launches as first private TV network
why: Founded by the Lebanese Forces militia, initially without a licence.

title: Casino du Liban closes during the war
why: Reopened in 1996.

title: AUB sets up Lebanon's first internet node
why: AUBnet became operational in 1993.

title: LBCI formed from LBC's assets
why: Current LBCI entity established 1992.

title: Lebanon's .lb domain created for AUB
why: Nabil Bukhalid administered it; he was inducted into the Internet Hall of Fame in 2017.

title: Audiovisual law legalises private TV and radio
why: Lebanon described as the only Arab country to do so at the time.

title: LibanCell claims first GSM call in Lebanon
why: Placed from the Alexandre Hotel, Beirut. Cellis launched the same year.

title: Lebanon connects to the internet; dial-up goes commercial
why: Commercial services began in 1995.

title: First ISPs licensed: Data Management, Terranet, Cyberia, Libanpac
why: Dial-up cost about $75 a month at 14 kbit/s.

title: Lebanon has 200,000 cellular users, most in the Arab world
why: Reported by Wikipedia's Internet in Lebanon article.

title: LBC launches satellite channel, first Arab satellite station from within region
why: LBCI went global with its satellite service.

title: Casino du Liban reopens
why: After a $50m reconstruction.

title: Beirut Stock Exchange relaunched
why: With an automated brokers system and Paris Bourse collaboration.

title: Lebanon has 40,000 internet subscribers
why: Almost half of all Arab internet users, per the article.

title: Berytech founded at Saint Joseph University
why: Listed as founded 2001; one brief suggested 2002. First technology pole in Lebanon.

title: Ethernet metropolitan network rolled out
why: Early broadband infrastructure step.

title: State cancels Cellis and LibanCell mobile contracts
why: Ended the 1994 exclusive arrangement; arbitration followed. Search summary only. Gulf News: government terminated the BTO contracts in June 2001; termination took effect 31 Aug 2002.

title: Charles Elachi, born in Rayak, becomes JPL director
why: Served until 30 June 2016; oversaw Curiosity, Kepler and Juno.

title: Cellis network renamed Alfa
why: FAL-DETE took over management under a four-year contract.

title: DSL introduced; ADSL launches in 2007
why: ADSL came after more than five years of delay.

title: ArabNet founded; Beirut hosts its first digital conference
why: Founded by Omar Christidis after he returned to Beirut in March 2009.

title: IMEWE submarine cable begins operating
why: Multiplied international bandwidth twentyfold; Ogero's page says operational 2009.

title: IMEWE capacity reaches consumers after ministry-Ogero dispute
why: More than eight months after the cable opened. Search summary only.

title: Alfa launches Lebanon's first 3G+ service
why: Another page says operators launched 3G in November 2011.

title: Beirut Digital District officially launches
why: ZRE, Berytech and the Telecom Ministry partnered in Bachoura.

title: Anghami launches in Beirut
why: Founded by Eddy Maroun and Elie Habib as a legal music-streaming alternative to piracy.

title: Fibre-optic backbone network completed
why: Wikipedia lists completion in 2013.

title: Alfa and Touch introduce 4G data services
why: First Lebanese 4G, starting in dense urban areas.

title: BDL issues Circular 331 for startup investment
why: Guarantees 75% of bank stakes in knowledge-economy firms and VC funds.

title: MEVP becomes first licensed VC under Circular 331
why: Raised $70m in 2014. Another source dates the circular's announcement to 2014. MEVP first BDL-licensed VC, raised $70m in 2014, compliant with Circular 331 (July 2014).

title: UK Lebanon Tech Hub starts; accelerator announced June 2015
why: Launched early 2015 at the Beirut Digital District, per Wamda. Wamda: hub started earlier in 2015; international accelerator announced June.

title: Speed accelerator at BDD: 3 months, $30,000
why: Start year of Speed not confirmed here. Speed@BDD: 3-month programme, $30,000; first batch 15 Sep 2015.

title: Toters delivery app founded by Khalfa and Halwani
why: Search summary only.

title: Nabil Bukhalid inducted into Internet Hall of Fame
why: Honoured for bringing the internet to Lebanon.

title: Circular 331: $368m approved, $203m executed, 9,000 jobs
why: Exits included Diwanee to Webedia and Shahiya to Cookpad; limit raised to $650m in 2016.

title: No national AI strategy or AI ministry found before 2020
why: Absence of evidence in searches, not proof; university AI labs may exist. Absence claim; ESCWA 2020 guide was requested by the ministry then, consistent but not proof.

title: Afiouni becomes Minister of State for Technology and Investment
why: In Saad Hariri's third cabinet; served to January 2020. Titles vary in word order. Cabinet formed 30/31 Jan 2019; Afiouni served to Jan 2020.

title: Banks close two weeks; liquidity crisis deepens
why: Crisis became apparent Aug 2019; later restrictions on dollar withdrawals hit all businesses.
